source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 7 (How do Organisms Reproduce?).

sections.heading: 1. Why and How Organisms Reproduce
points: **Reproduction** ensures continuity of a species and passes **DNA (genetic material)** to offspring.
**Variations** arise during reproduction — important for **evolution and survival** in changing environments.
Two modes: **asexual** (single parent, no gametes, offspring genetically similar) and **sexual** (two parents, gametes, variation).

sections.heading: 2. Asexual Reproduction
points: **Fission** — binary (Amoeba, Leishmania) or multiple (Plasmodium).
**Budding** — a bud forms and detaches (**Hydra, yeast**).
**Fragmentation** — body breaks into pieces that grow (Spirogyra).
**Regeneration** — lost body parts regrown (Planaria, Hydra).
**Spore formation** — spores in sporangia (Rhizopus/bread mould).
**Vegetative propagation** — new plants from roots/stems/leaves (potato eyes, Bryophyllum leaf, grafting, layering, cutting; tissue culture).

sections.heading: 3. Sexual Reproduction in Plants
points: **Flower** = reproductive part; **stamen (anther+filament)** = male (pollen); **carpel/pistil (stigma, style, ovary)** = female (ovules).
**Pollination** — transfer of pollen (self or cross; by wind, water, insects) from anther to stigma.
**Fertilisation** — pollen tube grows to ovule; fusion of gametes → **zygote**; ovule → seed, ovary → fruit.
Seed germinates into a new plant.

sections.heading: 4. Human Reproduction and Health
points: **Puberty** — physical/hormonal changes making the body capable of reproduction (secondary sexual characters).
**Male system** — testes (make sperm + testosterone), vas deferens, urethra, penis; **Female system** — ovaries (eggs + oestrogen), fallopian tubes (fertilisation site), uterus, vagina.
**Fertilisation** in oviduct → zygote → embryo implants in uterus → develops via **placenta**; **menstruation** occurs if no fertilisation.
**Reproductive health** — **contraception** (barrier: condoms; hormonal: pills; IUCD/Copper-T; surgical), spacing births; **STDs** (HIV-AIDS, syphilis) prevented by condoms.
Sex determination in humans: **XX = female, XY = male** (father's chromosome decides sex).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Budding = Hydra/yeast; fission = Amoeba/Plasmodium; regeneration = Planaria.
Vegetative propagation: potato eyes, Bryophyllum leaf buds, grafting, layering.
Fertilisation site in humans = fallopian tube (oviduct); embryo nourished via placenta.
Sex determination: XX female, XY male (father determines sex).
Copper-T = IUCD; condoms prevent STDs (HIV/AIDS).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Budding** = Hydra/yeast; **binary fission** = Amoeba (don't confuse).
Human **fertilisation occurs in the fallopian tube (oviduct)**, not the uterus.
**Father determines the sex** of the child (XY); mother always contributes X.
**Bryophyllum** reproduces by **leaf buds** (vegetative propagation).
